desktop.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop Dispatch agent-definition editor, revised design proposal.
Primary request: Design a beautiful restrained usable agent editor based on a critique calling for clear revision behavior, dominant instructions, installed capabilities, and separate project assignment.
Canvas: landscape 1536 x 1024 or larger, flat straight-on application UI. No device frame, perspective, browser chrome, decorative objects, or photography. Crisp legible Inter-like typography. White workspace, deep navy headings, pale blue-gray sidebar, restrained teal primary action, thin borders and modest radii. A tiny caption ABOVE the application frame reads "Dispatch · Revised editor concept". Caption is outside product UI.
Navigation: narrow dark navy rail with Dispatch D mark, Chats icon, Agents icon selected, Settings bottom. Pale sidebar titled "Agents": understated "+ New agent" button, Recovery Engineer selected, Archivist, Evidence Reviewer, Developer. Main white editor fills ALL remaining width. NO right-hand assignment panel.
Main composition: generous content margins, an uncluttered single primary form column, not an equal-weight card grid. Header breadcrumb "Agents / Recovery Engineer", title "Edit definition", quiet subtitle "Reusable expertise for any project." Header state "Based on revision 3" with small amber dot and text "Unsaved changes". 
Identity compact at top: "Name" input "Recovery Engineer"; "Description" input "Inspect old backups and recover verifiable files."
The dominant visual element is a large "Instructions" textarea, significantly taller than any other control. Its content is four clearly separated paragraphs:
"Purpose: Recover valuable files from old storage."
"Method: Inventory, inspect, verify, and preserve provenance."
"Deliverables: A recovery manifest, evidence, and unresolved gaps."
"Collaboration: Request independent review before declaring work complete."
Use comfortable readable text and plenty of editing space.
Below textarea a slim collapsed settings row with chevron: "Model" then "GPT-6 Astra · High" and a subtle "Change" control.
Below that a compact section "Capabilities", helper "Choose from capabilities available on this server." Show one selected checkbox row "Files and commands" with smaller description "Read, edit, and work with local files." Show a second unselected disabled row "Archive inspection" with a clear quiet amber outlined "Unavailable" status and helper "Not installed on this server." Do not show raw extension identifiers or separate Tools/Extensions pickers. No futuristic features.
Connections is a quiet read-only compact row with lock icon: "Connections" — "No connections assigned". Helper: "Managed by your administrator. Each connected service enforces access."
At bottom a softly tinted information strip: "Saving creates revision 4. Agents already in conversations keep their current revision."
Sticky bottom action bar aligned with form: left subtle "Discard changes", right single teal primary "Save revision 4". No other primary button anywhere. No Add to project on this screen.
Constraints: one dominant task, excellent visual hierarchy and readable contrast, all complete form sections and footer visible, no clipping, no internal SQLite terminology, no arbitrary numbered section badges, no repeated Proposed badges, no workflow, runner, memory policy, readiness or qualification controls. Do not put human photos or private account data into UI. This is an illustrative mockup, not proof of installed agents or implemented new controls.

assignment.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: separate desktop project-assignment interaction sketch for Dispatch.
Primary request: Show a focused project-side "Add agent" flow, separate from editing or saving reusable agent definitions. Use a SAVED definition revision only.
Canvas landscape, flat straight-on UI, high fidelity. Same restrained navy/aqua Dispatch visual system: narrow navy icon rail, pale conversation/project sidebar, white main workspace, Inter-like typography, clear contrast, thin borders, teal primary action. No device frame.
Outside the application, a quiet top caption reads "Dispatch · Project assignment sketch". A small outside footer annotation reads "Interaction proposal only. Assignment ownership and storage scope remain undecided." This annotation is documentation outside the product UI, not an end-user control.
App context: Chats selected in rail, sidebar "Conversations", "Home Photos" expanded and "Backup investigation" listed. Main area breadcrumb "Home Photos / Add agent". Header "Add an agent to Home Photos"; subtitle "Choose a saved definition, then describe the work."
Main centered form with generous whitespace and one clear vertical reading order.
Section "Agent": selected card "Recovery Engineer" with subtitle "Inspect old backups and recover verifiable files." and small text "Saved revision 4". A subtle secondary link "View definition" and select "Revision" showing "Revision 4 · Latest saved". Helper "Only saved revisions can be assigned."
Section "Work for this project": 
"Goal" multiline field "Find photos, email archives, and other useful old files."
"Inputs" reference picker with two file-style rows "Existing inventory" and "Restored objects"; subtle "Add reference" text action. References are concrete selectable resources, not a single ambiguous combined chip.
"Output location" selected reference "Home Photos / Recovery evidence".
"Collaborators" selected role rows "Archivist — classification" and "Evidence Reviewer — verification"; small helper "Participants available to this project".
"Constraints" textarea "Preserve originals and cite source locations."
Bottom info line "This assignment uses revision 4. Later definition edits will not change it."
Footer left "Cancel", right single primary teal button "Add agent". No Save revision button. No editable reusable instructions, no runner or model controls, no connection credentials.
Avoid equal-weight dense card grids, numbered section circles, or repeated proposal badges. Keep the app calm and grounded in a real workflow. Example agents and references are illustrative; no fake success state or claim of actual provisioning.

explainer.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram
Asset type: revised technical companion to the simplified Dispatch agent editor and separate assignment sketch.
Primary request: Accurately map the smaller user-facing editor to Pi Durable 1.0.1 storage and registered code; make revision semantics and the unresolved assignment contract explicit.
Portrait high-resolution infographic on white background, navy headings, teal accents, blue existing concepts, amber proposed controls, gray external code/resources. Exceptionally legible sans-serif with monospaced identifiers. Generous spacing, concise text, no decorative robots. No product navigation.
Title "From the revised editor to Pi Durable"
Subtitle "Engineering reference · Pi Durable 1.0.1"
Prominent principle "Configuration selects behavior. Registered code implements it."
TOP storage panel heading "SQLite: <stateDir>/pi.sqlite". Two connected boxes: "documents" with "Address + metadata" and "id · kind · scope_kind · owner_id · record"; arrow caption "id → document_id"; second box "document_revisions" with "Values + changes" and "document_id · content · kind · seq · version". Below: "Materialize latest base plus later deltas. documents.record is metadata."
Key directly below: "D = dispatch.catalog / agents[] / session scope" and "A = pi.agent / native conversation scope".
CENTER five-row table with columns "EDITOR" / "SAVED DATA" / "BEHAVIOR":
"Identity" / "D.name · D.description · D.revision" / "Reusable definition; revision created on save"
"Instructions" / "D.instructions → A.instructions" / "Combined with registered prompt sections; rendered changes become pi.system entries"
"Model" / "D.provider + D.modelId → A.model; D.thinkingLevel → A.thinkingLevel" / "Saved model configuration for each instance"
"Capabilities" / "D.extensions[] + D.tools[] → A.extensions[] + A.tools[]" / "Registry resolves executable code; selector and unavailable state are proposed"
"Connections" / "D.connections[]; dispatch.mcp-bindings; dispatch.mcp-catalog" / "Public metadata, binding keys and cached discovery; credentials remain outside SQLite"
Below table a clear "Save and use are separate" two-lane diagram.
Lane 1 "EDIT DEFINITION": "Unsaved edits → Save revision 4 → dispatch.catalog"
Lane 2 "USE SAVED REVISION": "Project-side assignment* → Select saved revision → Create participant and native conversation → Configure pi.agent"
Under lane2: "dispatch.shared-conversation.members[] pins agentDefinitionId + agentRevision."
Prominent notice: "Saving a new definition revision does not update existing participants."
Next an amber outlined box, heading "Assignment contract — still open". Text: "The sketch shows goal, input references, output location, collaborators and constraints. Decide ownership: participant, conversation or project. No assignment storage scope or schema is approved." Do NOT assert that assignment is a conversation-scoped native type.
Bottom two boxes:
"CAPABILITY SETTINGS — FUTURE" text "Add settings only when a registered capability implements them. No generic memory, runner, workflow or qualification fields are introduced by this revision."
"OUTSIDE SQLITE" text "Extension implementations · tools · ExecutionEnv code · agent-connections.json · credentials · source files and recovered artifacts"
Small footer: "Existing native task state uses tasks.record and state.checkpoint. A UI selector does not implement a durable workflow."
Legend "Blue: existing storage/runtime concepts · Amber: proposed interaction or unresolved contract"
Constraints: exact identifiers and spelling. Keep all text readable without dense clutter. Do not invent an agents SQL table. Do not serialize executable code into SQLite. The new capability picker and project assignment are concepts, not implemented features. This is a revised explainer, not an application screenshot.
